claims.claim: Twenty-six Starlink V3 satellites were deployed by Ship 41 twenty-five minutes after launch.
claims.episode_span: SpaceX released the first onboard image of the deployment sequence from one of the satellites. Twenty-six V3 satellites reached orbit twenty-five minutes after liftoff from Starbase.
claims.source_title: SpaceX shares first picture of Starlink V3 satellite deployment by Starship on debut orbital flight
claims.supporting_quote: The 26 satellites were released by the upper stage Ship 41 when it reached space about 25 minutes after launch from Starbase, Texas.

claims.claim: Each V3 satellite targets one Tbps downlink and one hundred sixty Gbps uplink.
claims.episode_span: Each V3 satellite masses approximately two thousand kilograms. The design targets one Tbps downlink and one hundred sixty Gbps uplink per satellite.
claims.source_title: Starlink Beamed Live Views From Orbit During Starship Flight 14
claims.supporting_quote: V3 satellites are designed to support 1 Tbps of downlink capacity and 160 Gbps of uplink — roughly a 10x improvement in downlink and a 22x increase in uplink compared to V2.

claims.claim: xAI's Colossus campus drew an average of eight hundred twelve thousand five hundred two gallons of water daily from the Memphis Sand Aquifer.
claims.episode_span: xAI's Colossus campus has drawn an average of eight hundred twelve thousand five hundred two gallons of water daily from the Memphis Sand Aquifer.
claims.source_title: Memphis Council Faces Final Vote on Data Center Pause as Rally Targets Musk
claims.supporting_quote: Environmental advocacy group Protect Our Aquifer reported that xAI pumped an average of 812,502 gallons of water daily from the Memphis Sand Aquifer for its Colossus 1 supercomputer.
